sanskrit: dhītī vā ye anayan vāco agraṃ manasā vā ye avadann ṛtāni | tṛtīyena brahmaṇā vāvṛdhānās turīyeṇa manvata nāma dhenoḥ ||
english: Those who by thought led speech to its summit, or who by mind declared the truths — waxing great through the third sacred utterance, by the fourth they perceived the name of the milch-cow.

sanskrit: sa veda putraḥ pitaraṃ sa mātaraṃ sa sūnur bhavat sa bhavat punarmaghaḥ | sa dyām aurṇod antarikṣaṃ sa svar viśvā bhuvo abhavat sa ābhavat ||
english: He, the son, came to know his father; he, the son, came to know his mother; he became a son, he became again a munificent one. He disclosed the sky, he the atmosphere, he the sun; he became all the worlds — he came into being.

sanskrit: atharvāṇaṃ pitaraṃ viśvadevaṃ mātur garbhaṃ pitaraṃ saṃyuvānam | ya īṃ ciketāmṛtasya dhāman nityasya rāyaḥ paridhīṃr apaśyat ||
english: The Atharvan as father, all-divine; the embryo of the mother, the father bringing together — he who discerned the abode of immortality, who saw the boundaries of eternal wealth.

sanskrit: śivās ta ekā aśivās ta ekāḥ sarvā bibharṣy ahṛṇīyamānaḥ | guhā vāco nihitās tisra etā eked idaṃ vi babhūvānu sarvam ||
english: Some of your forms are auspicious, some are inauspicious — you bear them all without anger. Three forms of speech are hidden in the secret place; from one of them all this world has spread forth.

sanskrit: aditir dyaur aditir antarikṣam aditir mātā sa pitā sa putraḥ | viśve devā aditiḥ pañca janā aditir jātam aditir janitvam ||
english: Aditi is the sky, Aditi the atmosphere, Aditi is the mother, he the father, he the son; all the gods are Aditi, the five peoples are Aditi; Aditi is what has been born, Aditi is what shall be born.

sanskrit: diteḥ putrāṇām aditer akāriṣaṃ mahāśarmaṇāṃ mahatām anarmaṇām | teṣāṃ hi dhāma gabhiṣak samudryaṃ naiṣāṃ vepasaḥ paro asti kiṃ cana ||
english: I have made praise for the sons of Aditi, the great sheltering ones, the great and unharmed ones. Their abode indeed is fathomless, reaching the sea; beyond their trembling power there is nothing whatsoever.

sanskrit: vājasya nu prasave mātaraṃ mahīm aditir nāma vacasā karāmahe | yasyām idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanam āviveśa sā no devī suhavā śarma yacchatu ||
english: At the starting of the vigorous race we shall invoke by speech the great mother, Aditi by name, in whom all this universe has entered — may that goddess, easy to invoke, bestow shelter upon us.

sanskrit: mahīm ū ṣu mātaraṃ suvratānām ṛtasya patnīm avase huvema | tuvikṣatrām ajarantīm urūcīṃ suśarmāṇam aditiṃ supraṇītim ||
english: The great mother of those of excellent vows, the wife of cosmic order — we would invoke her for aid: Aditi, of mighty dominion, ever-young, wide-reaching, granting fine shelter, of good guidance.

sanskrit: sutrāmāṇaṃ pṛthivīṃ dyām anehasaṃ suśarmāṇam aditiṃ supraṇītim | daivīṃ nāvaṃ svaritrām anāgaso asravantīm ā ruhemā svastaye ||
english: The well-protecting earth, the sinless sky, Aditi of fine shelter and good guidance — may we ascend the divine boat, well-oared, faultless and never leaking, for our well-being.

sanskrit: ekayā ca daśabhiś cā suhūte dvābhyām iṣṭaye viṃśatyā ca | tisṛbhiś ca vahase triṃśatā ca viyugbhir vāyav iha tā vi muñca ||
english: O Vāyu, well-invoked, you travel with one and with ten, with two and twenty for the sacrifice, with three and thirty — unyoke those here, release them now.

sanskrit: ayā viṣṭhā janayan karvarāṇi sa hi ghṛṇir urur varāya gātuḥ | sa praty ud aid varuṇo madhvo agraṃ svāṃ yat tanūṃ tanvām airayata ||
english: By this pervasion he generated glorious deeds; for that radiance is broad for choosing a path. Varuṇa rose up toward the summit of sweetness when he set his own body in motion within himself.

sanskrit: yajñena yajñam ayajanta devās tāni dharmāṇi prathamāny āsan | te ha nākaṃ mahimānaḥ sacante yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ santi devāḥ ||
english: The gods worshipped sacrifice with sacrifice — those were the first cosmic laws. Those great ones attend the vault of heaven where the ancient Sādhya gods abide.

sanskrit: yajño babhūva sa ā babhūva sa pṛthivyā adhipatir babhūva | sa pra jajñe sa u vāvṛdhe punaḥ so asmāsu draviṇam ā dadhātu ||
english: The sacrifice came into being; it fully came into being; it became lord over the earth. It was born, it grew again — may it establish wealth in us.

sanskrit: devā yad devān haviṣāyajant- -āmartiyān manasāmartyena | bravāma tatra parame vyoman vadema tad uditau sūryasya ||
english: When the immortal gods worshipped the immortal gods with an oblation, worshipped the deathless with a deathless mind — let us speak of that in the highest heaven, let us utter it at the rising of the sun.

sanskrit: mugdhā devā uta śunāyajant- -ota gor aṅgair bahudhāyajanta | ya imaṃ yajñaṃ manasānvavindat pra ṇo vocat tam iheha bravāma ||
english: The enchanted gods also worshipped with a dog, and worshipped with the limbs of a cow in many ways. He who by mind discovered this sacrifice — may he proclaim it to us; let us speak of him here and now.

sanskrit: yat puruṣeṇa haviṣā devā yajñam atanvata | kva svit tad adya no brūyād yadi havyenejire ||
english: When the gods extended the sacrifice with the primordial being as the oblation — who indeed today could tell us of that, if the oblation-offerers were actually set in motion?

sanskrit: indraḥ sutrāmā svavām̐ avobhiḥ sumṛḍīko bhavatu viśvavedāḥ | bādhatāṃ dveṣo abhayaṃ kṛṇotu suvīryasya patayaḥ syāma ||
english: May Indra, the good protector, self-strong, with his aids, gracious and all-knowing, be favorable; may he thrust away enmity and make us fearless — may we be lords of heroic strength.

sanskrit: sa sutrāmā svavām̐ indro asmad ārāc cid dveṣaḥ sanutar yuyota | tasya vayaṃ sumatau yajñiyasy- -āpi bhadre saumanase syāma ||
english: May that good-protecting, self-strong Indra keep enmity far away from us, away into the distance. May we be in the favor of that worshipful one, abiding in his auspicious goodwill.

sanskrit: yas te pṛthu stanayitnur ya ṛṣvo yo daivaḥ ketur viśvam ābhūṣatīdam | mṛḍayā no vidyutā deva sasyāya mota vadhī raśmibhiḥ sūryasya ||
english: Your broad thunder, your towering form, your divine banner that adorns all this world — be merciful to us, O god, with lightning for the crops, and do not strike us down with the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: yas te stanaḥ śasayur yo mayobhūr yaḥ sumnayuḥ suhavo yaḥ sudakṣaḥ | yena viśvā vanasi vāryāṇi sarasvatī tam iha dhātave kaḥ ||
english: That breast of yours, O Sarasvatī, that is richly nourishing, that brings delight, that is grace-giving, easy to invoke and full of skill — the one with which you win all desirable things, set that here for giving nourishment.

sanskrit: idaṃ te havyaṃ ghṛtavat sarasvat- -īdaṃ pitṝṇāṃ havirāsyaṃ yat | imāni ta uditā śaṃtamāni tebhir vayaṃ maghavānaḥ syāma ||
english: This oblation of yours, O Sarasvatī, mixed with ghee — this is the mouth-offering belonging to the ancestors. These most beneficent utterances of yours that have been proclaimed — by these may we become wealthy patrons.

sanskrit: prapathe pathām ajaniṣṭa pūṣā prapathe divaḥ prapathe pṛthivyāḥ | ubhe abhi priyatame sadhasthe ā ca parā ca carati prajānan ||
english: Pūṣan was born on the foremost of paths, on the foremost path of heaven, on the foremost path of earth. Knowing the way, he travels to and fro between both most beloved abodes.

sanskrit: pūṣemā āśā anu veda sarvāḥ so asmām̐ abhayatamena neṣat | svastidā āghṛṇiḥ sarvavīro +'prayucchan pura etu prajānan ||
english: Pūṣan knows all these directions; may he lead us by the most fearless path. A giver of well-being, shining bright, with all heroic power, never neglectful, may he go before us, ever knowing.

sanskrit: pūṣā gā anv etu naḥ pūṣā rakṣatv arvataḥ | pūṣā vājaṃ sanotu naḥ ||
english: May Pūṣan follow our cattle; may Pūṣan protect our horses; may Pūṣan win strength for us.

sanskrit: pūṣan tava vrate vayaṃ na riṣyema kadā cana | stotāras ta iha smasi ||
english: O Pūṣan, under your vow may we never come to harm at any time. We are your praisers here.

sanskrit: śukraṃ te anyad yajataṃ te anyad viṣurūpe ahanī dyaur ivāsi | viśvā hi māyā avasi svadhāvo bhadrā te pūṣann iha rātir astu ||
english: One of your forms is bright, another is worthy of worship; you have two forms of different appearance — you are like the sky. For you protect all creative powers, O self-powerful one. May your bountiful gift be here, O Pūṣan.

sanskrit: dhātā dadhātu dāśuṣe prāñcaṃ jīvātum akṣitam | vayaṃ devasya dhīmahi sumatiṃ satyadharmaṇaḥ ||
english: May Dhātṛ bestow on the pious man an undiminished, forward-moving life. May we hold in mind the good favor of that god whose law is truth.

sanskrit: dhātā viśvāni dāśuṣe dadhātu prajākāmāya dāśuṣe duroṇe | tasya prajā amṛtāḥ saṃ vyayantu viśve devāso aditiḥ sajoṣāḥ ||
english: May Dhātṛ bestow all things upon the pious man, upon the pious man desiring offspring, in his house. May immortal offspring clothe themselves about him; may all the gods and Aditi, with one accord, be favorable.

sanskrit: dhātā rātiḥ savitedaṃ juṣantāṃ prajāpatir nidhipatir no agniḥ | tvaṣṭā pūṣā prajayā saṃrarāṇo yajamānāya draviṇaṃ dadhātu ||
english: May Dhātṛ, Rāti, and Savitṛ be pleased with this; may Prajāpati, lord of treasures, our Agni — may Tvaṣṭṛ, delighting in offspring together with Pūṣan, bestow wealth upon the sacrificer.

sanskrit: dhātā prajānām uta rāya īśe dhātedaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ jajāna | saṃ dāśuṣe vahatu bhūri puṣṭā tasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
english: Dhātṛ rules over offspring and over wealth; Dhātṛ generated this entire universe. May abundant nourishment be conveyed to the pious man — to that god let us offer homage with an oblation.
